/data/api_link	https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/23497
/data/title	Wine Flask (Bian Hu)
/data/date_display	Han dynasty (206 B.C.–A.D. 220), 1st century B.C./A.D.
/data/place_of_origin	China
/data/description	This unusual variation of the canteen-shaped container is lightly chiseled with a combination of geometric patterns, birds, and gazelle-like creatures. The distinctive technique and style of surface decoration seen on this vessel associate it with bronzes excavated in far southern China, near modern Vietnam. Under occupation by Han rulers, bronze foundries in this frontier area produced intriguing bronzes in which Chinese styles are blended with those of the native, non-Chinese tribes.
/data/dimensions	22.5 × 26.3 × 8.3 cm (8 7/8 × 10 3/8 × 3 1/4 in.)
/data/medium_display	Bronze with incised decoration
/data/credit_line	Lucy Maud Buckingham Collection
/data/publication_history	Charles Fabens Kelley and Ch’en Meng-chia, Chinese Bronzes from the Buckingham Collection (Chicago: The Art Institute of Chicago, 1946), 138. Mizuno Seiichi, ed., Sekai bijutsu zenshū, no. 13: Chūgoku Qin–Han [The Arts of China: Qin and Han Dynasties] (Tokyo: Kadokawa Shoten, 1962), fig. 26. Chicago Bijutsukan Meihenten: Masterpieces of Chinese Arts from the Art Institute of Chicago, exh. cat.
